CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke just told opposition parties to stop contesting elections because they are rigged. Read that carefully. If elections are genuinely rigged the solution should be fixing the electoral process. But CJP's solution is to boycott elections entirely.

So how does the government change then?

Through the streets. Exactly the way BNP used violent protests in Bangladesh to overturn a government rather than winning through the ballot box. The template is not subtle. And the country recognises it.

But there are questions CJP never answers.

When Punjab had a paper leak under Congress, CJP was silent. When Jharkhand had a leak, CJP was silent. But when anything happens under BJP the protests are instant. EVM problems only appear when BJP wins. When the opposition won Punjab and Himachal the EVMs were apparently working perfectly.

That is not consistency. That is selective outrage designed to serve a specific agenda.

Then there is the funding question nobody in mainstream media is asking.

36 days of protests at Jantar Mantar. Stage, logistics, sound systems, crowd management, media coordination. None of that is free. Who paid for it?

CJP's co-convenor Saurav Das lives in a GK-1 luxury apartment at 9 to 10 lakh rupees per month in rent. For an NGO worker that money has to come from somewhere. Where exactly?

• You may have already seen him online being trolled and targeted with derogatory slurs like Meetha, Chakka, Hijda, and worse.

• He understands the pain and frustration of the 22 lakh students and their families affected by the paper leak, as well as the millions of others who have suffered because of more than 89 major exam paper leaks across the country.

• As a queer individual fighting for his rights, visibility, and existence in a deeply transphobic and homophobic Indian society, he has likely faced immense struggles himself. Yet despite that, he chose to show up for others.

• He may have participated in protests before too, something that many educated and socially aware people never do in their entire lives.

• From these videos, one thing is clear: he has a great sense of style and carries himself with confidence.

• He is socially aware, respectful, politically conscious, and unafraid to speak about rights, justice, and issues that matter.

• Meanwhile, lowlifes hiding behind fake profiles chose to mock and ridicule him for doing something I would call an act of genuine courage.

body:
I want to take a moment to thank Abhijeet Dipke.
For 19 days now, he has been teaching this nation a masterclass.

Not in exam reform.
In something more valuable.

He flew in from Boston. Unemployed.
To save India's students.

Then handed the mic to Allah.
Kashmir.
RSS.
Umar Khalid.

Wait.
Where is Dharmendra Pradhan?

Well. 
He is not generating any TRP.
And he is having fun continuing as Education Minister.

Turns out the fastest way to save a minister's job is to hire professional protestors.

Pradhan should be sending flowers to Jantar Mantar.
Maybe Pradhan hired Abhijeet Dipke.

Nobody even remembers his name is on the placards anymore.

Special mention to Sonam Wangchuk.
Came for a guest appearance.
Stayed to become the whole show.

19 days without food. Visibly.
While everyone else on that stage eats on schedule.

And the menu is incredible.

Continental on Monday.
Chinese on Tuesday.
Hyderabadi on Wednesday.
American on Thursday.
Repeat.

With desserts.
Tea.
Coffee.

Imagine fasting for 19 days next to a buffet you're not invited to.

Every speaker walks up.
Says a few lines about Allah.
Ambedkar.
Kashmir.
RSS.
Umar Khalid.
Then walks off to eat.

Wangchuk stays.
Hungry.
Foolish.
Watching.

Wondering if anyone even remembers what this started as.
At some point even the most patient man starts doing math.

If Wangchuk could speak freely right now. 
Off the record.
We suspect it would not be about the education ministry.
It would be about catering.

Here's the real service Dipke has done this country.
He has finally taught us how to spot a cockroach.

Not the ones NEET aspirants are competing against for a medical seat.
The ones standing on a stage at Jantar Mantar.

Holding a mic.
Talking about everything except the paper leak that started this.
And still don't know who is President of India.

The real students are indoors.
Revising.
Silent.
Unheard.
The stage belongs to everyone else now.

So thank you, Abhijeet Dipke.
You didn't get Pradhan to resign.
You got India to forget why he should.

That takes talent.

I first met @AshutoshRanka two months ago, when the NEET paper leak controversy had just erupted, well before the CJP was formed. He had painstakingly compiled data on every major paper leak in India over the last two decades and sent it to me on WhatsApp. The research was meticulous and deeply impressive.

Little did I imagine that this same young engineering graduate would soon be sitting across the table from two Union ministers, negotiating on behalf of student protesters.

As he told me, he had never even been to Jantar Mantar before this. Ashutosh isn’t a professional agitator. He’s an idealistic young Indian who chose to act.

I interviewed him last night after the CJP-government talks. He looked exhausted, seemed unwell, but spoke with remarkable clarity and conviction.

If there’s one lesson from the last few weeks, it’s this: never underestimate the power of informed, idealistic youth. You don’t have to agree with everything Ashutosh says but cannot but admire his spirit. Watch: https://t.co/81PxIP0Izo

AISA president Neha Bora did not whisper.
She said it plainly:
“The hardships we have endured under BJP-RSS rule, we will make you face all those hardships in return.”
This is not a slogan written in an air-conditioned studio.
This is a student who sat on a 23-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar, watched paper-leak politics destroy futures, watched young people get called terrorists and viruses, and still refused to look away.
She is not asking for a cabinet reshuffle.
She is saying the wound is deeper than one minister. The project is BJP-RSS itself — the politics that turned neighbours into enemies, classrooms into battlegrounds, and dissent into a crime.
Defeat them in elections, she says.
Then defeat them at the tea stall, in the classroom, on WhatsApp, in memes, in songs. Leave them no soil.
Youth movements are not asking for mercy anymore.
They are asking for memory.
And they are promising return.
#NehaBora #AISA #GenZ

Today, under the banner of the India Alliance Student Organizations, student organizations including NSUI, AISA, SFI, AISF, MSF, Samajwadi Chhatrasabha, and CRJD participated in a press conference. They collectively voiced their strong opposition to the government’s anti-student policies, which are threatening the future of India's youth and the integrity of the education system.

This protest is a direct response to the Modi government's failures on:

⚠ 𝐔𝐆𝐂 𝐃𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐭—A threat to academic autonomy

⚠ 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬’ 𝐔𝐧𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐄𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬—Silencing student voices

⚠ 𝐍𝐄𝐏—Pushing privatization at the cost of accessibility

⚠ 𝐒𝐨𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐉𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐞—Failing marginalized students

⚠ 𝐏𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐤 𝐒𝐜𝐚𝐦—Destroying students' futures

In view of the above, the India Alliance Student Organizations will lead a historic march at Jantar Mantar, bringing together educationists, India Alliance leaders, teacher organisations, student leaders, and students from across the country. The details of the proposed march are mentioned below👇

𝐃𝐀𝐓𝐄: 24 March 2025

𝐓𝐈𝐌𝐄: 11 am

𝐕𝐄𝐍𝐔𝐄: Jantar Mantar, New Delhi

The India Alliance Student Organization remains committed to ensuring social justice, campus democracy, and access to quality education for all. The fight for students’ rights will continue until the government addresses these urgent concerns.
